exposure: Type of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) (3a/3b vs 3c/4th degree)
Advice given regarding mode of delivery
outcome: Women's preference for mode of delivery (MoD) in a subsequent pregnancy
cohort: 100 consecutive women who sustained an obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) and were attending postnatal follow-up at a perineal trauma clinic.
finding: Women with 3c/4th degree obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) are more likely to prefer a planned caesarean section, while for women with 3a/b OASI, sexual symptoms have the greatest impact on preferred mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Women with 3c/4th OASI are more likely to accept a planned caesarean section, whereas sexual symptoms are the commonest factor influencing caesarean preference in women with 3a/b OASI.
cross-section timing: During postnatal follow-up at a perineal trauma clinic.
